newsitem.title: USA: Westell sees Q3 loss of $0.10-$0.12/shr.
newsitem.headline: Westell sees Q3 loss of $0.10-$0.12/shr.

text.p: Westell Technologies Inc said Friday it expects to report a loss of $0.10 to $0.12 a share for its fiscal third quarter, worse than analysts' estimates.
The company said third quarter revenues will likely be about $17 million.
Westell said it expects to post revenue growth in the fourth fiscal quarter versus the third and a corresponding reduction in losses.
According to First Call, the consensus of analysts' estimates was a profit of $0.05 a share for its third quarter ending December 31, versus a loss of $0.02 last year.

"(Fiscal third quarter) Westell revenues will be in the $17 million range, and losses will be in the range of $0.10-$0.12 per share, which will be below analysts' current expectations," Westell said. "We expect to see sequential revenue growth in the final fiscal year 1997 quarter and a corresponding reduction in losses."

Westell said third quarter revenues from Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) technology will be less than it expected because of the upcoming introduction of its FlexCap Rate Adaptive (RADSL) system, due in fiscal fourth quarter.

Westell said the company is also monitoring the potential that FlexCap Phase III piece part inventories supporting the current ADSL systems become obsolete, leading to a possible writeoff of obsolete inventories and purchase commitments.
"In a worse case scenario, this could result in a one-time charge in the range of $0.07 to $0.09 per share," Westell said.
"However, we are actively pursuing various options to mitigate this potential writeoff," the company said.

Westell said its base business of other communications products is likely to be flat in the December quarter compared with the prior year and sequentially down somewhat from the near-record September quarter, as a result of the typical year-end spending patterns of its customers.

"We do anticipate sequential improvement in base business in our March fiscal quarter, and our cost reduction efforts should begin to be reflected in that quarter as well," the company said in a statement.
The new RADSL platform includes a faster online connection than the previous system, symmetric or assymetric operation, can be upgraded with software and requires less power to run.
"We expect (it) will be the first fully commercially scaleable product at a sub-$1,000 cost per home served," Westell said, adding however that customers are willing to wait for for it.
"The normal evaluation of the new RADSL system by our customers, coupled with the production ramp up, will impact total shipments in the March fiscal quarter as well," Westell said.

Westell said recent partnership announcements with Northern Telecom Ltd and Sourcecom, and its Access Multiplexer Beta trials beginning this month involving 13 customers in nine countries, will require continued and even increased expenditures for product and market development.
"The already significant levels of investment we are choosing to make in these areas will increase sequentially for the foreseeable future," Westell said.
